key_insight: In chaotic dynamical systems, distributional reinforcement learning can be better conditioned than standard value-based RL because the return distribution evolves more smoothly than individual trajectories under the 1-Wasserstein metric.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a more stable learning objective for control and optimization problems in science and engineering domains where chaos makes expected-return RL highly unstable.
method: Analyze RL in chaotic systems through the geometry of return distributions rather than scalar value estimates.
Use the 1-Wasserstein distance to show that distributional Bellman updates can remain smoother under chaos.
Provide a principled theoretical explanation for why distributional methods may outperform standard RL when trajectories diverge rapidly.
evidence_signal: The paper is primarily theoretical: the abstract reports a mild statistical stability assumption and a 1-Wasserstein analysis, but does not mention experiments or benchmark data.
watch_item: The claimed advantage depends on statistical stability assumptions, so practical gains may weaken if the system violates those assumptions or if the Wasserstein-based update is expensive to estimate.
paper_title: On Distributional Reinforcement Learning in Chaotic Dynamical Systems
